clips.text: This is the one part of the whole module that is openly defensive. Most of it stays small: a headache, a question at the pharmacy counter. But the same four moves scale up to a real emergency, so we build them here, while the stakes are still low.
Me duele la cabeza.
At the pharmacy counter, name the pain before asking for anything. Speak now.
¿Desde cuándo le duele?
Duration is the first thing a pharmacist actually needs, not a diagnosis. Keep it to one clean answer.
Desde ayer.
The pharmacist asks since when. Answer with one clean phrase: since yesterday. Speak now.
Le recomiendo este para el dolor.

Here is the wall. Since 2010, a Mexican pharmacy cannot sell an antibiotic without a prescription from a doctor licensed in Mexico — and a prescription from your own country will not be accepted at this counter. Asking first saves you an argument you cannot win.
¿Necesito receta para este medicamento?
Before you take anything to the till, ask whether this medication needs a prescription. Speak now.
No, este no necesita receta.
One more filter before you buy, and it connects back to B13. If you have an allergy, the pharmacy counter is not exempt from that sentence.
Tengo una alergia. ¿Tiene algo sin aspirina?
You cannot take aspirin. Say so and ask for an alternative. Speak now.
Sí, este es con paracetamol.
Now the scale-up. Same four moves — name it, give it a timeframe, ask the constraint, get the answer — but the object is a real emergency, and the phone is the counter.
911, ¿cuál es su emergencia?
Someone next to you has collapsed. Call and say you need an ambulance. Speak now.
Necesito una ambulancia.
¿Cuál es su ubicación?
911 is the number for the whole country: ambulance, police and fire, all through the same door. Give the address you already made portable back in B04 — this is exactly what it was for.
Give your location using the hotel name and room number. Speak now.
Estoy en el hotel, en la habitación trescientos cinco.
Vamos en camino.
Me duele la cabeza. ¿Necesito receta para este medicamento? Necesito una ambulancia.

B17 complete. Name the problem. Give it a timeframe if asked. Ask the constraint before you hit it — receta, alergia. And if it scales up: 911, the ambulance, the address you already had ready. The only defensive part of the module, and now it is four short moves, not a fear.
A traveller describes a headache at the pharmacy, checks the prescription rule and later calls for real help. Listen for the same four-move pattern at two different scales.
Me duele la cabeza. Desde ayer.
Le recomiendo este para el dolor.
¿Necesito receta para este medicamento?
No, este no necesita receta.
Necesito una ambulancia. Estoy en el hotel, en la habitación trescientos cinco.
Vamos en camino.
